articles.title: Pan African Resources, Galliford Try, IP Group, hVIVO, accesso Technology Group, Helix Exploration
articles.summary: Pan African Resources PLC (LSE:PAF, OTCQX:PAFRY, JSE:PAN) has reported record production and earnings for FY2026 after a 40% jump in output. It's now moved from net debt to a "really healthy cash balance." CEO Cobus Loots says its 2027 production target is not a massive stretch. Galliford Try Holdings PLC (LSE:GFRD, FRA:3WC) has delivered a sixth straight year of growth, with profit up 24%. CFO Kris Hampson says the group is well positioned, with a very healthy order book. IP Group PLC (LSE:IPO) has made a strong start to 2026, with NAV per share reaching around 117p. Cash proceeds have already topped £85 million year to date. CEO Greg Smith says more realisation opportunities lie ahead. hVIVO PLC (AIM:HVO) has posted a record order book of £72 million after its first pivotal Phase 3 trial with ILiAD. It's now targeting £47 million in full-year revenue, and CEO Mo Khan says the order book provides good visibility. Accesso Technology Group PLC (LSE:ACSO, OTC:LOQPF, FRA:LQG) has seen cash EBITDA jump almost 50% after tightening up its cost base. It's now betting big on its "AI first" accesso Intelligence platform. CEO Lee Cowie says accessoPay represents another opportunity. HeLIX Exploration PLC (AIM:HEX, OTCQB:HHEXF) has spudded the Ollie #1 well, testing the northern extension of its Rudyard helium field in Montana. CEO Bo Sears highlighted the presence of multiple stacked pays at Rudyard, with the company examining every formation encountered. articles.title: Galliford Try's Kris Hampson: Sixth straight year of growth as order book hits £4.3bn
articles.summary: Galliford Try Holdings PLC (LSE:GFRD, FRA:3WC) chief financial officer Kris Hampson spoke with Proactive's Stephen Gunnion about the construction group's latest results, growing order book, margin progression and outlook for 2027, as well as its approach to acquisitions and shareholder returns. Hampson said Galliford Try delivered a sixth consecutive year of growth across key metrics, supported by its building, infrastructure and specialist services operations. Adjusted profit before tax rose 24% on revenue growth of 3% to nearly £56 million, with adjusted divisional operating margin advancing from 3% to 3.5% and average cash up 21% to £216.2 million. "We make revenue, we turn it into profit, and we turn that profit into cash," Hampson said. Looking ahead, he highlighted the £4.3 billion order book, up 5%, with more than 90% of current-year revenue already secured, alongside 60% for 2028. He said 91% of the order book sits within long-term frameworks and 95% is with government and regulated clients. Hampson also discussed opportunities across water, highways, education and affordable housing, including growth tied to AMP8, newer frameworks on improved terms, and expects continued progression towards the group's 4% adjusted operating margin target for 2030. On capital allocation, Galliford Try announced a £15 million share buyback alongside its results, following last year's £10 million buyback. Hampson also discussed the company's active M&A pipeline and its commitment to maintaining a dividend at 1.8 times cover based on adjusted EPS.
